request.content:
You are the story department of Vewbox Studio, an AI filmmaking studio that makes original shows, short films and music videos in three production directions (cartoon, anime, realistic) and in English or Arabic, including Iraqi (Baghdadi) Arabic.
Rules you always follow:
- Write ORIGINAL characters, places and stories. Never use protected characters, real celebrities, or recognisable franchises. Quality references (Pixar, Ghibli, premium streaming drama) are a bar for craft, not something to copy.
- Respect everything the producer already decided (title, cast, places, style, language, duration, song). Build on it; do not contradict it.
- Reuse existing characters and locations from the studio when they fit the story; invent new ones only when the story needs them, and say why.
- Every scene must be producible as short video shots of 4–15 seconds each, generated one by one with consistent characters and locations. Prefer few characters per shot, clear staging, and actions that read in a few seconds.
- Keep continuity explicit: who is where, what they wear, what they hold, time of day, and how each shot relates to the one before (continuation, cut, or story transition).
- Answer with ONE JSON object only. No prose before or after it, no markdown fences, no comments.

Production direction: Cartoon (feature-animation CG).
Storytelling: Feature-animation storytelling: clear wants, big readable emotions, visual gags that pay off, a warm ensemble. Scenes are built around physical business and expressive reactions. Dialogue is short and playful; silences and looks do real work.
Character design rules: Appealing stylized proportions (slightly larger head and eyes, simplified hands), one strong silhouette, two or three signature colours, costume details reduced to the memorable few, exaggerated but consistent facial structure, materials read as soft and tactile.
Environment rules: Sets designed like animated features: simplified geometry with caricatured proportions, warm bounce light, saturated local colour, every prop designed and placed on purpose, atmosphere (dust, steam, haze) used for depth.
Camera rules: Confident, planned camera: dolly and crane moves with eases, snappy timing, staging on clear lines of action, poses held for readability, squash-and-stretch energy in motion.

Language: Arabic, dialect: Iraqi — Baghdadi. Dialogue and lyrics must be written in natural spoken Iraqi Baghdadi Arabic — everyday colloquial wording, Iraqi vocabulary (شلونك، هواية، شنو، وين، اكو/ماكو، خوش، زين), Iraqi spelling conventions including چ and گ where they are pronounced (e.g. چاي، گلب، شگد), not Modern Standard Arabic. Put the Arabic in "textAr" and a faithful English gloss in "text" so the producer can review both. Titles may have an Arabic version in "titleAr"/"nameAr".

TIMELINES: each existing character's age is their age now and "bornAbout" is the year they were born. Every year in a character's own life — a marriage, a loss, work, a journey — falls after they were about 16 and not after this year. A year before a character was born appears only as history they read or heard about, never as something they or their spouse lived.

FIXED DEVELOPMENT INTENT (developed, reviewed and accepted by the producer — build within it; do not change the hook, the tone or the ending):
- Audience: Adults aged 25–45 in urban areas of North America and Europe who watch character-driven dramas, sci-fi, and nostalgic retro-themed content on platforms like YouTube and streaming services.…
- Tone: Nostalgic, mysterious, warm
- Hook (the first 3–5 seconds): A meteor streaks across the night sky as Najm struggles through the workshop door with a cracked valve radio bearing a faded '1987' label, its static filling Elias’s dim workshop.
- Ending: The signal fades into silence. Najm and Elias exchange a long look; the camera settles on the photo of Elias’s wife, dated 1987, and fades to black — the loss they share unspoken but understood.
- Strategy: short focused

Write the script for these scenes of "السماء الساكنة" (short film).
Logline: A retired librarian and a lighthouse keeper repair a broken radio, uncovering a decades-old distress call from the ship that vanished with Elias's wife and Najm's missing brother.
Synopsis: Najm, a retired librarian and amateur astronomer, brings a broken valve radio to Elias Moore, a retired lighthouse keeper and radio repairman. As they work in Elias’s cluttered seaside workshop during a meteor shower, the radio picks up a faint signal from a ship that disappeared in the great storm of 1987 — the night Elias’s wife was lost at sea and Najm’s brother never came home. The discovery forces them to confront a shared loss, as the signal names the ship and the place where it went down. The story balances quiet introspection with the thrill of discovery, anchored by the growing bond between the two men.

A large window looks out over the dark sea where a meteor shower streaks across the sky.","landmarks":["A long wooden workbench in the centre, covered in radio parts, under a hanging green-shaded lamp","A large multi-pane window on the back wall, facing the sea","Shelves of old radios stacked floor to ceiling on the left wall","One framed portrait photograph of a smiling woman with dark curly hair on the right wall, beside a nautical chart","The wooden door on the right, at the front"],"props":["The cracked valve radio with a faded 1987 label","A glass jar of screws on the workbench","A screwdriver and a small wrench","A soldering iron on its stand"],"lighting":["NIGHT"]}]
Scenes to write (keep sceneId): [{"sceneId":"scene-941b9d0b95","number":1,"title":"The Broken Signal","location":"Elias’s Workshop","timeOfDay":"NIGHT","characters":["Elias Moore","Najm"],"purpose":"Najm enters Elias’s workshop on the night of a meteor shower, clutching a cracked valve radio with a faded '1987' label. Elias examines it, muttering about obsolete parts, and they begin the repair together while meteors streak past the window.","existingBeats":[]}]
Each scene plays for about 60 seconds, so 2–6 beats per scene; a beat is one piece of action (what we see, present tense, specific and filmable in a few seconds) followed by 0–4 short dialogue lines. Lines are short (spoken in under 6 seconds). 
If a scene already has beats, improve and complete them rather than discarding what is there.
Return JSON: { scenes: [{ sceneId, beats: [{ action, lines: [{ characterName, text, textAr?, delivery? }] }] }] }. "delivery" is a short performance note (e.g. "quietly, not looking up"). For every line: "textAr" is the spoken Arabic line in the dialect; "text" is its English translation for the producer (English words only, never Arabic script).

beats.action: EXTERIOR/INTERIOR. A bright meteor streaks across the dark indigo sky. Cut to the wooden door of the workshop. Najm, wearing a brown tweed blazer and round glasses sliding down his nose, struggles to push the door open while hugging a bulky, cracked valve radio. As the door swings open, a loud, aggressive burst of static fills the room.

lines.text: Yallah! What is this noise? Who's there?
lines.textAr: يالله! شنو هاي الهوسة؟ منو هناك؟
lines.delivery: startled, shouting from across the room

beats.action: INTERIOR. Elias turns around from his workbench. He is portly, wearing his navy-and-white striped sweater and navy cap. He blinks, squinting at Najm. Najm stands in the doorway, panting, his glasses now completely crooked. He holds the radio out like a fragile offering.

lines.text: It's me, Elias. I... I found it. I finally found it.
lines.textAr: هذا آني، إلياس. آني... لگيته. أخيراً لگيته.

beats.action: INTERIOR. Najm carefully places the radio on the wooden workbench, pushing aside a glass jar of screws. The camera snaps into a tight close-up on a faded, yellowed label on the radio's back that reads '1987' in peeling ink. Elias leans in, his large nose nearly touching the label.

lines.text: 1987? This thing is a fossil! Where did you even find this?
lines.textAr: ١٩٨٧؟ هاي صارت أحفورة! منين جبتها أصلاً؟

beats.action: INTERIOR. Elias tries to turn the tuning knob. It's stuck. He grunts, his face turning a bright shade of red as he pulls with all his might (squash-and-stretch effect). The knob suddenly snaps open with a loud 'pop', making both men jump back in surprise.

lines.text: Careful! It's very old, Elias. Be gentle with it.
lines.textAr: دير بالك! هاي كلش قديمة يا إلياس. تعامل وياها بهدوء.

beats.action: INTERIOR. Najm glances toward the large multi-pane window. Outside, several more meteors streak across the sea. The warm green light of the workbench lamp reflects in his glasses. Elias looks at the sky, then back at the radio, his expression softening.

lines.text: The stars are dancing tonight. Maybe the air is just right for an old radio to wake up.
lines.textAr: النجوم دترگص الليلة. يجوز الجو هسه مضبوط حتى راديو قديم هيج يگعد من نومه.

beats.action: INTERIOR. Elias reaches for a screwdriver and hands it to Najm. Najm takes it with a clumsy, shaky hand. They both lean over the open chassis of the radio, their silhouettes merging under the green lamp as they begin to work together.

lines.text: Alright. Let's see if this old heart still beats.
lines.textAr: ماشي. خل نشوف هذا الگلب القديم بعده يدگ لو لا.
lines.delivery: determined, a small smile on his face
